reviews.comment: Great professor. The lecture topics are important but at the time are somewhat mundane which made it difficult for me to pay attention in class, but I was able to teach myself the material from her slides alone. She is great about answering questions outside of class. There are few homeworks but they are really long, dont put them off like I did.

The course material is not that hard to me, but you need to really spend time to learn it. Quizzes are annoying, you need to prepare for it every week. The good things are if you tried homework, you will get full credit, no matter the answer is right or wrong. Also she curved the class, my rough grade was 84/100, but I still get an A at the end.

She is basically Jesus incarnate. Some professors refuse to help you out of "fairness" (basically laziness honestly), but Dr. Welch will do everything and anything to make sure you understand the concepts, and will even walk through your code on the weekend to help with a project. Her lecture notes are some of the most concise and useful ones ever.
Dr. Welch is a very kind professor. Her office hours are very helpful for the projects. Study for the weekly quizzes and you'll be fine. Lots of free points and curved the final grade.

Welch was honestly pretty good for 222. She was pretty good at using the slides as a starting point and the white board to make sure we understood a concept. Her tests were doable, but the homeworks took a lot of time, so beware. She curves pretty significantly, as I didn't think I got close to an A, but still got one.

Everything is so unnecessarily strict. I'm supposed to be learning here but you get punished for ridiculous things on the homework and quizzes, (which btw there are way too much of) and it frustrates me. I like the material coming from a math background but this is just ridiculous. It makes it unbearable to learn. It sucked.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Welch genuinely cares for her students and if you put in the time and effort, she is more than happy to help you. I failed both midterms and almost every in-class quiz, but going to office hours every week and asking questions (VERY important!), I managed to get an A in the class. Overall is the hardest class I have taken at TAMU thus far.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Welch is a great professor! Not to mention that she is in charge of honors, she really knows how to teach. She teaches clearly and knows the content very well. I really recommend her!
Dr. Welch is really nice and is a caring professor. She really knows the material and does a good job conveying it. Overall, I hope to take her again as a professor in the future.

She puts in a lot of effort in preparing Quiz and homework material. This means you will end up with Quizzes and HWs every week of semester including spring break. She writes important things on whiteboard but her speed of explanation is way fast for undergrads. Exam grading is strict with no time to think so you end up cramming just to pass.

I honestly didn't enjoy taking CSCE 121 with Dr. Welch. She went at a super fast pace for what's supposed to be an intro level class and I found myself lost most of the semester. It took all of my energy just trying to get almost impossible assignments turned in on time. She's great if you have CSCE experience, otherwise consider another professor.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She's a really good prof for CSCE121. She gets a little fast when she thinks there are things we should already know, but if you ask questions she'll slow down. She's a little quirky (especially if you try to email her), and can come off as rude, but overall she's a really nice lady who cares a lot about her students and her work.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: She is extremely knowledgable in her domain. Along with this, she is very supportive and approachable to students, and very nice human being too. Felt priviledged in attending her class.
Very knowledgable about the material being covered. Her programming assignments would sometimes require multiple visits to the TA or her office.
